# Decide

This page tells how the `decide` slice of the core plugin `claudetto` lets Jev pick an option for a question of Claude.
A user reads it to turn the feature on or off.
A contributor reads it before an edit of `slices/decide/`.

## The Concept

Claude sometimes asks the user a question with `AskUserQuestion` when facts can settle the answer.
Jev is a model of the TypeSafe API.
The slice sends such a question to Jev and adds the pick of Jev to the matching option.
Claude and the user then see the pick and its confidence.
The user still answers the question.

A question about a goal, a preference, or an approval stays as Claude asked it.

## It Is Off by Default

The plugin option `decide` has two values:

| Value | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `off` | The default. The plugin sends no request to Jev. |
| `jev` | Jev picks. The question goes to the TypeSafe API. |

The value `jev` needs the env var `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` when Claude Code starts.
If the key is not set, the call passes unchanged.
Only the value `jev` sends data to the TypeSafe API.

## The Hook

The slice adds one `tool.call` hook on `AskUserQuestion`, in the phase `rewrite`.
One call costs one request to Jev.
The hook does these steps:

1. It picks each question that has 2 or more options and is not multi-select.
2. It asks Jev two things for each such question: the kind of the question (`facts` or `preference`), and the best option.
3. It adds the note `Jev picks this option (confidence N).` to the description of the picked option.

The hook changes a question only when both answers have a confidence of at least `MIN_CONFIDENCE` (0.5), the kind is `facts`, and the pick is one of the options.
The text of the question does not change, because the answers come back with that text as key.
If Jev gives no answer, or the run fails or times out, the question stays as Claude asked it.

## The Command

The hook runs the command `claudetto-decide` with Bun.
The key goes in the environment of the process and never in the arguments.
The command is also usable alone:

| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `claudetto-decide yes "<question>"` | Prints `P(yes)` for a yes or no question. |
| `claudetto-decide pick "<question>" key[=description]...` | Prints the chosen key, the confidence, and the probability of each key. |
| `claudetto-decide ask` | Reads one JSON object on stdin with `questions` and `state`. Prints the answers as JSON. |

`yes` and `pick` take `--state <text>` for facts, `--state -` to read the facts from stdin, and `--json` for a JSON output.
A `--` ends the flags.
The state is text and never a file path, because a path would send a file to the API.
A `pick` question has `MIN_OPTIONS` (2) to `MAX_OPTIONS` (255) options.
The output adds a line when Jev is not sure: a confidence under 0.5 for `pick`, or `P(yes)` within 0.2 of 0.5 for `yes`.

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | An answer. |
| 1 | A failure. |
| 2 | A usage fault, such as a missing key or question. |
| 3 | The key is not valid (status 401). |
| 4 | The account has no balance (status 402). |

When the command fails, it prints the error and the hook leaves the question as Claude asked it.

## Bounds

All bounds are in `slices/decide/limits.ts`.

| Bound | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `JEV_TIMEOUT_MS` | 45,000 ms for the whole run of the hook. |
| `ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS` | 12,000 ms for one try. |
| `TRIES` | 3 tries on a reply of 429 or 529. |
| `BACKOFF_MS` | 1,000 ms before the first retry. Each later wait doubles. |
| `ERROR_BODY_MAX` | 200 characters of an error body. |
